🗺️ The 53: every player on exactly one themed team of about 10

The whole league is split by facts that never change: where he was born, height, birth year, debut, draft slot, path to the NBA and pedigree. Every split is a real yes/no question, so each team's recipe is its identity. No current teams, salary or minutes, so trades don't break it. Each player also gets a phonetic code you can read aloud: metro or country · height · debut · draft round · initials.

🃏 Pitch teams: "can I interest you in…"

Each team is 5 to 8 players: a starting five (two guards, two forwards, a center when the team has one) and up to three on the bench. Big groups split into divisions, like Caribbean Dawgs Hispaniola and Islands. Each player's own code comes from things that never change: birth region · height in inches · debut year · initials. Within a team, sort by any fixed fact to see what separates them.

Pick a player → his 10 closest "on paper" twins

Similarity uses standardized distance on the chosen numbers. Salary compares on a log scale, and players with no listed salary are matched without it. Stats are left out on purpose.

The cascade: every player lands in exactly one box

The questions run in order. The first yes takes the player off the board: International → NBA family → Physical extreme (7'0"+ or under 6'3") → Blue blood → Grinder (undrafted / 2nd round) → Twilight (32+ or $100M+ on record) → whoever is left, split by age and salary. Usage rate is left out because it's a stat.

▦ The player box score: six facts, each split into 10 equal slices of the league

Each column lines up every player in the league and cuts them into 10 equal groups. The lit cell shows which tenth he's in, and the label says exactly where. ⭐ My Stack: your dozen

Tap ☆ Add to my stack on any player card. Your stack is saved in this browser.

👀 Worth following: who's interesting right now, and why

The score is built only from facts and minutes: age, minutes trend, draft slot and salary, international ties, injuries, team changes, efficiency in limited minutes, and stat superpowers. Each card spells out why.

🔁 Moves since opening night

Trades are confirmed against reporting. Signings and releases are found by comparing ESPN rosters from Oct. 30 with today's, so exact dates are approximate. Today's rosters may still lag the newest moves.

🧬 Hidden superpowers: who's a statistical freak for his position

Each player is compared with his own position group (guards vs. guards, bigs vs. bigs). σ = standard deviations above the group average, so 2σ means about the top 2-3%. Charges drawn and shots off the dribble aren't in box scores yet.

Teams that need offensive rebounding

📈 Worth following: who's getting more of the game (2026-27 vs. 2025-26)

Usage = shots, free throws and turnovers per 36 minutes, a simple box-score version of usage rate. Needs 3+ games this season and 10+ last season. It's early in the season, so read the trend, not the number.

Dimension 2: Stats Lab · PER, true shooting, plus-minus, threes · 2026-27 vs. 2025-26

PER is Hollinger's formula computed from ESPN box scores. It's adjusted for pace and scaled so the league average is exactly 15, so it can differ slightly from Basketball-Reference. Source: ESPN box scores via the sportsdataverse mirror, updated daily. Last game included: . Each bar is one game: the full bar is attempts and the dark part is makes.

🔥 Standout performances: role players, career highs, splash nights

Flags: career high (points, rebounds or assists), role-player pop (under 22 MPG, scored 10+ above his average), splash (6+ threes), triple-double, defensive havoc (7+ steals and blocks combined). Built from the box scores, the same kind of nights @EveryBucketNBA and @rolepIayerperf post about.
